question: From which direction do the magnetic lines emerge?
solution:
The correct answer is the** __North Pole.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The direction of the glamorous field is taken by convention that the field lines crop from the **North pole and blend at the South pole.**
 
• The strength of a glamorous field can be observed from the degree of closeness of the field lines.
 
• Magnetic field lines appear to move from the South pole towards the North pole inside a magnet.
 
• Magnetic field lines start from the North pole and end up at the South pole.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Magnetic lines of force are imaginary lines that represent the direction of the glamorous field as we move from one pole to the other.
 
• Magnetic field lines are a visual tool used to represent glamorous fields.
 
• The four parcels of glamorous field lines are as follows
 
 
• They're unrestricted and non-stop curves.
 
• They're directed from the north pole outside the attraction towards the south pole of the magnet.
 
• The digression at any point on a field line gives the direction of a glamorous field at that point.
 
• Parallel and equidistant filed lines represent an invariant glamorous field. The earth’s glamorous field in a limited space is invariant.
